page: Microsoft Azure E8ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity stands at 64.0 GB of RAM, equating to an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. Attached storage includes 472 GB of local NVMe SSD, while no dedicated GPU hardware is provisioned. The CPU features comprehensive instruction extensions, including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and INT8).

Benchmark results demonstrate dependable mid-tier computational and memory throughput alongside specialized strengths in data compression. The instance delivers 2227.18 on stress-ng single-core and 9040.34 on multi-core operations, accompanied by a PassMark CPU score of 16243.12. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 85.42 GB/sec, while write bandwidth measures 37.89 GB/sec. Data manipulation tasks reflect solid execution, highlighted by single-threaded gzip compression at 35.21 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 14.51 GB/sec, placing in the top quartile of recorded scores.

Database and transactional testing indicate 4308.02 on PassMark database operations and 15.64 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads. LLM inference capabilities on CPU yield 767.53 prompt processing tokens per second on small 135M parameter models and 63.85 tokens per second on medium 7B models. Overall, the combination of 64.0 GB RAM and 472 GB high-speed local NVMe storage provides strong resource density for caching platforms, relational databases, analytics tasks, and memory-intensive enterprise services.
